trustBoundaries.description: Flutter/Dart application code, bundled resources, public configuration, and runtime memory on a user-controlled device
SharedPreferences and application-support files, including progress, transaction/recovery metadata, recovery snapshots, settings, and local diagnostics
Third-party Google Mobile Ads SDK and its network endpoints; current bootstrap initializes the SDK while AdService request/load/show operations are separately gated
Approved CI/external secret store for release signing and production release credentials
Future first-party backend boundary; no backend is currently integrated

networkPolicy.certificatePinningRationale: No first-party authenticated backend exists yet; revisit when one is introduced.
futureBackendRules: no reusable privileged secret embedded in the client
privacy inventory update before enabling new data flows

knownGaps.securityImpact: Google Mobile Ads SDK initialization is not yet gated by production consent/regulated-region state even though AdService request/load/show operations honor ENABLE_ADS.
ENABLE_DIAGNOSTICS is not yet an effective bootstrap gate for the local logger; diagnostics remain redacted and local-only and there is no remote crash-reporting SDK.

threats.scenario: Attacker decompiles or inspects APK/AAB/IPA resources and Dart/native code to recover configuration or logic.
mitigations: Treat all shipped client configuration as public
Never embed reusable privileged secrets
Inject signing/service credentials only from approved secret stores
Use the VERIFIED ENG-010 secret policy and REL-006 signing procedure as release controls
threats.residualRisk: Game logic and public identifiers remain inspectable by design.

threats.scenario: User or malware alters SharedPreferences/application-support files to change progress/economy state, transaction journals, reward ledger state, recovery snapshots, settings, or diagnostics.
mitigations: Validate and normalize persisted values on load
REL-004 preserves a local pre-repair snapshot before supported corruption repairs
SHOP-002 and REW-007 use validated absolute-state journals and idempotent recovery to avoid duplicate debit/grant after interruption
ECON-005 fails closed on corrupt or future economy schema markers
Do not treat client-side values as authoritative for future server rewards
threats.residualRisk: Offline single-player progress and local recovery metadata can still be modified on rooted/jailbroken devices; current controls target safe behavior and idempotency, not tamper-proof storage.

threats.scenario: Attacker modifies and redistributes a repackaged build or hooks runtime behavior.
mitigations: REL-006 keeps release signing keys and passwords outside source control
Official distribution relies on platform signature verification
No client-side integrity check is treated as an authorization boundary
threats.residualRisk: Unofficial modified builds remain possible outside trusted distribution channels.

threats.scenario: Network attacker observes or modifies traffic to third-party or future first-party services.
mitigations: Require TLS for declared network communication
Disallow application-owned cleartext traffic
Use scoped/expiring tokens and server-side authorization for any future authenticated backend
Require privacy/threat-model review before adding a new network processor
threats.residualRisk: Third-party SDK endpoint security remains partly controlled by the processor/platform; there is no first-party authenticated backend today.

threats.scenario: Credentials leak through source, build config, logs, screenshots, diagnostics, CI output, or artifacts.
mitigations: ENG-010 repository secret-hygiene CI guard and policy
SecretRedactor before diagnostic persistence/copy
REL-006 release-input preflight keeps signing/private credentials out of Dart defines and source
Rotation is required after suspected exposure
threats.residualRisk: Unknown credential formats may evade pattern-based redaction; callers must avoid logging secrets and SEC-002 dependency/artifact scanning remains pending.

threats.scenario: Runtime errors expose tokens, user-specific paths, private keys, or sensitive context, or diagnostics are enabled more broadly than intended.
mitigations: Central SecretRedactor runs before memory/file/debug/clipboard/runtime broadcasts
Diagnostics remain local-only in the current product and no remote crash-reporting SDK is integrated
PRIV-001 inventories the local diagnostic flow and deletion path
ENG-013 owns the ineffective ENABLE_DIAGNOSTICS bootstrap gate and any future remote reporting boundary
threats.residualRisk: Unexpected sensitive formats may appear in third-party exception text, and the local logger currently installs regardless of ENABLE_DIAGNOSTICS.

threats.scenario: A Flutter/native dependency introduces vulnerable code, unexpected data collection, or malicious build behavior.
mitigations: Dependencies remain explicit in pubspec and lockfile
PRIV-001 blocks selected unreviewed analytics/cloud/crash SDK additions until inventory review
Secret, privacy, security, and asset CI guards run before build
threats.residualRisk: Automated vulnerability/license scanning and dependency governance remain incomplete until SEC-002 and ENG-006 are verified.

threats.scenario: Malformed persisted values, transaction/reward journal payloads, recovery metadata, asset/config metadata, route actions, or repeated UI events produce crashes, stale decisions, or duplicate state mutation.
mitigations: Typed asset/economy configuration validates structured inputs
RecoveringPreferences validates and repairs supported corrupt local values while preserving a pre-repair snapshot when possible
SHOP-002 and REW-007 validate journal keys/values and replay absolute final state instead of deltas
ECON-005 rejects corrupt/future economy schema markers before reward/shop recovery
Navigation and gameplay actions use duplicate/race guards
Missing/corrupt assets have bounded fallbacks
threats.residualRisk: Future external/deep-link/network inputs require dedicated validation as they are introduced.

threats.scenario: Google Mobile Ads SDK initializes or processes data before required consent, or advertising behavior is mistaken for first-party offline processing.
mitigations: Google Mobile Ads is explicitly declared as the only current network processor in PRIV-001
AdService request/preload/load/show operations honor AppBuildConfig.enableAds
Release configuration rejects Google test ad-unit IDs
ADS-007 remains the blocking owner for production consent and regulated-region gating before SDK initialization and requests
threats.residualRisk: Current bootstrap still initializes MobileAds independently of the AdService request gate, so SDK initialization is not yet consent-gated until ADS-007 is verified.
